title: Keloids and hypertrophic scars
summary: Raised scars from excess collagen: hypertrophic scars stay within the wound and often settle; keloids spread beyond it, persist and recur after excision. Silicone and steroid first; procedures are specialist.

what: A **hypertrophic scar** is a raised scar that stays **within** the original wound and often improves over 1–2 years. A **keloid** is firm scar tissue that grows **beyond** the original wound border, persists and often recurs after excision.

list: Excess collagen production with reduced breakdown during wound healing.
Triggers: acne, piercing, surgery (especially under tension), burns, vaccination, minor trauma.
**Keloids** are much more common in **skin of colour** and run in families.

head: Hypertrophic scar
Keloid
rows: Earlobes, jawline, chest, shoulders, upper back

diagnosis: Clinical. Biopsy only for an atypical, rapidly growing or ulcerated ‘keloid’ (exclude dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans or other tumour).

head: Look-alike
Distinguishing clues
rows: Slowly enlarging plaque without a clear injury: biopsy
Purple papules in old scars; systemic signs

list: Prevention: avoid elective procedures (piercing, cosmetic surgery) on keloid-prone sites in people with a keloid history.
**Silicone gel or sheet** (OTC) for months, not weeks; pressure (earlobe pressure clips).
Potent topical steroid under occlusion for early raised scars.
Specialist: **intralesional steroid**, cryotherapy, pulsed dye laser, careful excision with adjuvant therapy (**high recurrence** after excision alone).

management: Explain that the aim is **improvement, not removal**.
red_flags: A rapidly growing or atypical ‘keloid’: exclude a tumour.
Keloid tendency or skin of colour before elective procedures: experienced operator only.
pearls: Keloids extend beyond the wound; hypertrophic scars do not.
OTC silicone gel is a reasonable first step for early raised scars: months, not weeks.
